questions.title: No-Semicolon Print
questions.description: Write a program that prints "HELLO SCET" without using a single semicolon in the main code.
questions.adminNotes: Classic trick: use printf's return value as an if-condition so the block needs no trailing statement semicolon, e.g. int main(){ if(printf("HELLO SCET")){} }. No reference .c file requested for this one.

questions.title: Debug the Program
questions.description: This program is meant to read N integers, print their sum, then print the array in reverse — but it contains 10+ planted bugs (syntax, logic, and runtime). Find and fix as many as you can — points are awarded per bug correctly fixed.
questions.adminNotes: Reference fixed solution: questions/solutions/bonus_1_solution.c. Bugs: 1) 'void main()' -> 'int main()'. 2) 'scanf("%d", n)' missing '&'. 3) 'int arr[n]' missing semicolon. 4) 'i <= n' -> 'i < n' (out of bounds). 5) 'sum + arr' -> 'sum + arr[i]'. 6) 'Sum' -> 'sum' (undeclared/case). 7) reverse loop 'i = n' -> 'i = n - 1' (out of bounds). 8) 'printf("%d ", arr[i])' missing semicolon. 9) 'printf("\nSum is positive")' missing semicolon (new in this revision). 10) if/else bodies have no braces. 11) 'else;' stray semicolon detaches the else body, so 'Sum is non-positive' always prints.

questions.adminNotes: Reference correct solution: questions/solutions/code_completion_1_solution.c. Correct order: B, H, A, C, F, E, G, I, J, K, D, L.
